I also tried to add
LDP_RDF_SOURCE
instead of
FEDORA_SKOLEM

, but this did not work, possibly because of the "dynamic" typing used to map LDP Types to Fedora Resource Events.  I guess that this is an ontology question, and particularly what types can be used as an event filters.

There is no difference in how messages are produced between queues and topics. The issue you are encountering relates to an assumption made by the fcrepo-triplestore-indexer, such that it expects the "single subject rule" to be in effect. I.e. that all triples will contain the same subject (including hash URIs). BNodes, of course, break that expectation.

The solution is to either 1: don't use BNodes or 2: index your triples into named graphs (this would involve writing your own triplestore indexer or waiting until someone else writes one – I'd like to at some point, but it's not high on my priority list).

OK.  So, the "single subject rule" explains why I see a difference when I change the DefaultFilter to include FEDORA_SKOLEM because a unique event is produced for the creation of the skolem subject triple, which is a single subject, that otherwise would not exist.
So, I am still not clear on why these indirect subject triples are indexed with a topic and not a queue?  Can you point me to the code where this "assumption" method is?

Since I can still use the topic for my use case, this rule bug does not really impact me, until I need to manage the flow with a queue.  Also, since I am not distributing messaging across separate hosts, (currently), this reduces the probability of a network issue, and consequently the benefits of a queue. I want to use the queue, though.
Indexing into named graphs is a definitely a solid idea.  Even beyond this issue, this should probably exist.  I will take a look at it.

First, however, I am also going to begin writing this API-X extension that JP2 encodes repo sourced binaries tomorrow, (a priority, for me).  I will start with just one encoding output type (kdu jp2) for one input file.  I anticipate modelling it directly on your image convert example, which is exactly what I need, except rather than use convert, it will use kdu_compress.
I decided to just write a triplestore indexer that puts each Fedora resource into it's own named graph. The result is here:
https://gitlab.amherst.edu/acdc/repository-extension-services/tree/master/acrepo-connector-triplestore

and it is available in the Sonatype snapshot repository, if you'd like to give it a try. I have it deployed in our Fedora system now, but I'd like to give it at least another week to test this before cutting a release.
So far, it seems to work great with Fuseki – indexing resources into small named graphs and then querying the union graph when querying across resources.
Thanks.  I will check it out.

I have been studying your (awesome) work with repository-services since Friday, and trying with some success to replicate the API-X developer tooling (i.e. build and load maven local published feature bundles from karaf in a docker container).  This definitely works, but for some reason (network latency?) the feature:repo-add mvn:... does not always work on a container build, even if the feature jar is there, and this was very puzzling. The order of the local and remote repos in the docker file seems to matter as well (local first).  I also had some trouble with the docker-compose container start timing as my feature container was not waiting for apix to start.  I finally resolved this by using the docker-compose 2.1 healthcheck that forces the feature container to wait for a healthy condition report from the apix container.
So, I have now gotten it to work so that the service executes kdu_compress when a request like
http://localhost/services/025.tif/svc:encode
is made.  However, the console log reports this:

encoder      | 2017-03-01 20:25:47,216 | ERROR | qtp161958430-82  | ExecProducer                     | 61 - org.apache.camel.camel-exec - 2.19.0.SNAPSHOT | The command ExecCommand [args=[-jp2_space sRGB, -i, -, jp2:-], executable=kdu_compress, timeout=9223372036854775807, outFile=null, workingDir=null, useStderrOnEmptyStdout=false] returned exit value 255

I am not sure about how kdu_compress handles stdin compared to convert, so the " - " stream argument syntax may not be consistent.  Maybe I have to concatenate the input "-i"," - " arguments into "-i -"?   Camel exec has no specific argument symbol for the input stream, I guess.

BTW, one other issue that i noticed is if triplestore-indexing is enabled and the API-X proxy is used for REST, then the indexer will use the event message resource URI and not be able to resolve it back to the "internal" URI.  So, for example, if I put a file at
http://localhost/fcrepo/rest/file.jpg,
then camel will try to resolve
http://localhost/fcrepo/rest/file.jpg
and not the FCREPO_BASEURI at
http://fcrepo:8080/fcrepo/rest/file.jpg

.  The question of external host names vs. container names in docker makes the proxy messaging implementation quite confusing.  Aliasing an external hosts name to the fcrepo container is a work around, but it will not remap the port from 80 to 8080.
This is a bit orthogonal to the issue described here, but w/r/t the hostname mapping, yes, it becomes really complicated. I would recommend taking a look at this note:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox#note,
which is pretty much what I have in place in our Fedora instance. You just have to ensure that
all
traffic to Fedora passes through that proxy, which is much easier if you completely isolate Fedora on its own server – it's much harder if you have clients/services accessing Fedora over the
localhost
interface.

BTW, one other issue that i noticed is if triplestore-indexing is enabled and the API-X proxy is used for REST, then the indexer will use the event message resource URI and not be able to resolve it back to the "internal" URI. So, for example, if I put a file at
http://localhost/fcrepo/rest/file.jpg,
then camel will try to resolve
http://localhost/fcrepo/rest/file.jpg
and not the FCREPO_BASEURI at
http://fcrepo:8080/fcrepo/rest/file.jpg

. The question of external host names vs. container names in docker makes the proxy messaging implementation quite confusing. Aliasing an external hosts name to the fcrepo container is a work around, but it will not remap the port from 80 to 8080.

regarding this, can you tell me what flavor of Docker you are using?  Is it a "Docker for [Windows|Mac|Linux]" or a docker-machine variety?  We have noted different behaviors in the accessibility of Docker network interfaces between the different flavors, and we're working on some patches to make things more seamless between them.
Linux
Docker version 1.13.1, build 092cba3
docker-compose version 1.10.0, build 4bd6f1a

Thanks, yes, accessibility of the networking interface sounds like a reasonable explanation for feature:repo-add fails.  It is also much slower generally to do a feature:repo-add in a docker container than directly in a Karaf on the host.
Definitely.  On my dev server, I currently reverse proxy all docker instances that use localhost:port to subdomain vhosts.  (so that
http://localhost:8080
= dor.example.org,
http://localhost:3030

= ts.example.org).  So, the camel cfg fcrepo.baseUrl just has to match the external (reverse proxied) domain name for the API-X proxy localhost:80, and the API-X proxy name question is solved for indexing.  For local development, it is a bit different, I guess.  I will just only use the baseUrl interface for CRUD interaction with fcrepo locally as a rule.

An update on the JP2 encoder feature based on acrepo-exts-image.  Since kdu_compress cannot read an InputStream, I just decided to build ImageMagick with the jp2 delegate.  I did not know that this was possible, but since ImageMagick is a standard tool, and I would rather depend on it than a closed source library.  If you are interested, the feature docker image is
here

I am using acrepo-exts-image with only one modification, and that is setting DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT = "jp2";  If this were in the configuration file, I could use your jar directly, rather than publishing a new one.  Please advise, as I am not that familiar with the best practices for Maven Central (and how to deal with very similar, but not identical implementations).

I am testing it now using Loris and the Universal Viewer.  It seems to work.  I am using Loris' template HTTP resolver.  One feature that could be useful is a prefetch "reindexer" that gets all of the images from the service and populates the loris jp2 cache.  This would improve initial load times.
w/r/t the output format, the existing code
should
support arbitrary output formats via the
Accept
header, so long as that header starts with
image/
. So, sending a request with this header:
Accept: image/jp2
should work right now.

sure, great idea, but I would have to write new resolver logic for Loris to send variable `Accept` headers to acrepo-exts-image depending on source format foreknowledge criteria specified from the client.  The process question is from where does the image server determine what resource format it is requesting and what format it is producing.   The obvious answer is from the image viewer client (via a manifest object), but this is not SOP, yet.  In the case of JP2, there are also distinct server decompression methods for the same content type, so the image server/client should theoretically also add its supported decompression method (e.g. kakadu or openjpeg) in the request.

In the IIIF manifest, a resource is required to have a source format, and a service definition for the image server request.  The right place for the content-type specification for the Accept header would be in a manifest service definition, imo.  (Though, this also is a bit complicated, because there are two distinct image server responses, the default IIIF API info.json image server service response (JSON-LD) and the resource binary serialization that is produced from a full IIIF URI.)

The viewer client then processes the service definition and it requests from the image server a resource with an Accept header, and then the image server would handle a viewer client specified format by resolving it against an appropriate Fedora API-X service (and also passing its own Accept header).

Image viewer clients (and consequently the servers) are generally quite liberal about content-type (format) requirements, and AFAIK none of them are implementing conneg.  Currently, Loris just reads the content-type from the response and then passes it to a handler rather than asking for it explicitly.  It seems that it wants to be able to handle every possibility.  I have previously addressed the relevance of conneg to the IIIF
here
I personally agree with enforcing a more stringent protocol on the client regarding (mandatory) Accept headers, but they seem to view it as more of "unnecessary complication".
The neat thing about API-X is that a particular encoding format can be wired into the service directly, and templated URIs can be made for each format, perhaps.  So, for example a TIFF resource at <
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/001.tif
> can have multiple service URIs, like <
http://localhost/services/001.tif/svc:jp2
> or <
http://localhost/services/001.tif/svc:png
>, and the template resolver would make an image service URI like <
http://localhost:5004/jp2:001.tif
> or <
http://localhost:5004/png:001.tif

>.  The prefixes jp2: and png: simply identify IRI templates that append the /svc:jp2 or /svc:png contexts on the request URI.  While having an image service be able to process multiple output formats is a brilliant implementation, maybe it is easier to make these services a bit less flexible and bound to a SOLID design pattern.
thanks for the context! I think the simplest thing would be for me to just change the code in the
acrepo-ext-image

so that the default format is configurable. Plus, I've been wanting to get a new release out, so I'll make that part of the update. If I have time, I'll do that today; otherwise, look for a new version on Maven Central early next week.

I have cut a 1.0.10 release of the Amherst repository extension services with both the updated (named-graph-based) triplestore indexer and the image service with more configuration options. The artifacts are now available on Maven Central.
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing.  It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.

I am testing an ActiveMQ queue in a "standalone" configuration and I have noticed that there is a difference in the way that fcrepo-triplestore-indexer consumes these messages from a queue instead of a topic.   Basically, any triple with a subject skolem/bnode is not consumed/updated with a queue, but is with a topic.  Object skolems are indexed in both cases.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Change jms.xml to use JmsQueuePublisher.
2. Insert into container a skolem type graph. (e.g. <> <
http://iiif.io/api/presentation/2#hasImageAnnotations
http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#first
http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type
http://www.w3.org/ns/oa#Annotation
3. Check indexing.

I have paused the indexing consumer so that I could see the messages in the ActiveMQ queue.  As expected, there is only one message queued for the modification of the parent container.  I noticed that the number of Camel exchanges with a topic versus a queue was more (6 vs. 3).   With a topic, 2 messages are produced in activemq for the above example, but a queue only produces one.
Since it is not possible to get the second two triples from the parent container using a URI like
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test2?preferInclude=PreferMinimalContainer&accept=application/rdf+xml,
I am guessing that a topic must include more messages, particularly relating to the creation of the bnode/skolems.
According to the
http://fedora.info/spec/#message-data,
a Skolem, being an LDPR should produce events.  But it seems that
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/observer/DefaultFilter.java
does not include it as a type.

I am testing an ActiveMQ queue in a "standalone" configuration and I have noticed that there is a difference in the way that fcrepo-triplestore-indexer consumes these messages from a queue instead of a topic. Basically, any triple with a subject skolem/bnode is not consumed/updated with a queue, but is with a topic. Object skolems are indexed in both cases.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Change jms.xml to use JmsQueuePublisher.
2. Insert into container a skolem type graph. (e.g. <> <http://iiif.io/api/presentation/2#hasImageAnnotations> _:c14n18 .
_:c14n18 <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#first> _:c14n12 .
_:c14n12 <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/ns/oa#Annotation> .)
3. Check indexing.

I have paused the indexing consumer so that I could see the messages in the ActiveMQ queue. As expected, there is only one message queued for the modification of the parent container. I noticed that the number of Camel exchanges with a topic versus a queue was more (6 vs. 3). With a topic, 2 messages are produced in activemq for the above example, but a queue only produces one.

Since it is not possible to get the second two triples from the parent container using a URI like http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test2?preferInclude=PreferMinimalContainer&accept=application/rdf+xml, I am guessing that a topic must include more messages, particularly relating to the creation of the bnode/skolems.

According to the http://fedora.info/spec/#message-data, a Skolem, being an LDPR should produce events. But it seems that https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/observer/DefaultFilter.java does not include it as a type.
